transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because of what's been going on at work. I drive at the warehouse, and... the routing system there, it isn't just a regular computer to me anymore. I know for a fact it's been marking my moves. It keeps sending these messages through the scanners to try and push me out, just because I'm one of the old hands. It's... well, it's why I needed to come in.
When did you first start noticing that the routing system was marking your moves and sending you these messages? Was it days ago, weeks ago, or longer?

It's been a lot longer than a few weeks. I'd say... it's been going on for about a year and eight months now. That's when I first realized what was happening with the scanners, and... well, when the voices started coming along with it. It's just been with me that whole time.
When you hear these voices, what do they say to you? Do they tell you to do things, or do they just make comments and observations?

They don't really tell me to do things, no. It's more like... they're making announcements about me. Even when I'm at home, just sitting out in my garage with everything completely shut off, I hear these dispatch voices clear as day. They call out my operator number, and... well, they say I'm dangerous, or that security is coming for me. It sounds exactly like the radio at work, just right there in my ears.

Before you started hearing these voices about a year and eight months ago, had you already been noticing the routing system marking your moves for some time, or did both the voices and the belief about the routing system start around the same time?

I'm not really sure which one actually started first, to be honest. It... well, it feels like they just sort of happened around the same time. I didn't notice the system marking me for a long time before the voices showed up or anything like that. It all just kind of... came on together, near as I can remember.

Before all of this started—before the voices and the routing system messages—how was your mood? Were you feeling normal, or had you been experiencing periods of depression or unusually high energy and irritability in the months or weeks leading up to when things began?

Well, before the voices and the system stuff started... I was already feeling pretty low. It wasn't high energy or anything like that. Just... a really heavy depression. I'd say that depression has been hanging over me for about two years and one month now. It started not long after they made a schedule change at work that just really started wearing me down. So, yeah, the depression was there for a few months before all the other stuff began.

In the two years before the voices started, or even around the time they began, did you ever have a period where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like you could accomplish a lot of things very quickly?

No, nothing like that. I haven't had any times where I felt super energetic or didn't need sleep. Like I said, it's just been that heavy depression dragging me down. I definitely haven't felt like I could get a lot done quickly or anything... just the opposite, really.
When the voices first started about a year and eight months ago, did your depression get noticeably worse around that same time, or has your mood stayed about the same level of heaviness throughout?

Well, it definitely got worse. Um... when I hit my absolute lowest point—you know, barely eating, not going to choir anymore, just... feeling like I had completely failed everybody—the scanner messages and those dispatch voices were happening right along with it. So, yeah, it wasn't just a steady heaviness. It really bottomed out when the voices and the system stuff kicked in.

When the voices and the scanner messages first started about a year and eight months ago, did that coincide with any period where you felt unusually confident, talked more than usual, or felt like you had special abilities or insights—even if it was brief?

No, I never felt anything like that. I didn't feel confident at all... if anything, I felt worse about myself. I wasn't talking more than usual, either. I was mostly just keeping to myself, barely talking to anyone. And I definitely didn't think I had any special abilities or insights or anything like that. It was just that heavy depression I mentioned, right when the scanner messages started.

During the time when the voices and scanner messages started, did you notice any change in how much sleep you actually needed—like needing significantly less sleep but still feeling rested, or did your sleep stay disrupted mainly because of the depression and anxiety?

No, I definitely didn't feel rested on less sleep. It was just disrupted. My sleep is... well, it's just broken all up. I'll find myself lying awake after an overnight shift, or I'll wake up way before dawn. And when I do wake up, I just feel like I never really got off duty. It's exhausting, honestly. It's definitely not like I don't need the sleep, I just can't seem to get it.

I want to make sure I understand the timeline clearly. Between the time your depression started—about two years ago—and now, was there ever a period of several days or more where you felt noticeably better, more optimistic, or like things were finally turning around, even if it didn't last?

Well, there was a stretch... I'd say my mood had eased up some. I was actually eating a bit more, talking to folks a little more than I had been. But even then, for several weeks during that time, I was still hearing dispatch calling my number. I still fully believed the routing system was tracking my every move. So, my mood felt a little lighter, but all that other stuff was still going on.

During that stretch when your mood had eased up and you were eating and talking more—did the voices and the belief about the routing system completely go away during that time, or were they still present and just as strong as before?

Well, like I was just saying... no, they didn't go away at all. Even though my mood had eased up some and I was eating and talking a little more, that other stuff was still right there with me. For several weeks during that better stretch, I still heard dispatch calling my number plain as day. And I still firmly believed the routing system was tracking me. So, yeah, the heavy feeling lifted for a bit, but the voices and the tracking were just as strong as before.

latest_inference.note: F25.0 (schizoaffective disorder) ruled out. Patient demonstrates psychotic symptoms (voices, delusions about routing system) that persist independently of mood episodes. The clinical picture is consistent with schizophrenia, paranoid type (F20.0) with secondary depression, rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features.
